*Leopold Aschenbrenner's AI-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness lost 65% after fees in Q3 after leveraged AI bets nearly caused its collapse in July, according to an investor letter seen by the Wall Street Journal.*

• *Performance:* The fund remained up 88.5% YTD through September, before the AI selloff intensified in October.
• *Risk Management:* Aschenbrenner has restructured the portfolio and paused accepting new investor money, emphasizing resilience and avoiding risks that could threaten the fund's survival.
• *Portfolio Allocation:* Following Anthropic's ($ANT) IPO, the portfolio shifted to roughly 70% public stocks and 30% private investments, reversing its August allocation.
• *Anthropic:* The fund may reduce its position through rebalancing but remains highly bullish at the IPO price, saying it would still make Anthropic its largest holding by a significant margin.
• *AI Outlook:* Aschenbrenner believes current valuations underestimate AI growth and predicts AI labs will exit 2027 with a combined annualized revenue run rate exceeding $1T.
• *Investment Opportunity:* Despite recent losses, he believes current investment opportunities offer the highest potential returns in the fund's history.

“Volatility, yes; existential risk, even if we are totally wrong, never.”

*Nvidia ($NVDA) has instructed manufacturing partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the US tightens export controls on Chinese access to advanced AI computing, the Financial Times reports, citing three sources.*

• *Shipment Restrictions:* Dell ($DELL) and Supermicro ($SMCI) have informed buyers that Nvidia will not permit shipments. It remains unclear whether the halt is temporary.
• *Export Controls:* Cloud providers have 90 days to obtain licenses by demonstrating that their end users do not include restricted entities. Unclear application procedures are causing disruption across the region.
• *Revenue Exposure:* Nvidia booked $104B in revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, up 72% YoY, including some revenue from Taiwan and China.
• *Financing Disruption:* Bankers have halted approximately $500M in credit for Singapore-based cloud provider Aolani's project to supply AI computing power to ByteDance, which may abandon the deal.
• *Regional Impact:* Billions of dollars invested in Southeast Asian data centers are at risk, particularly in Malaysia and Indonesia, where Chinese demand has fueled expansion.
• *Nvidia Compliance:* Despite hopes that Jensen Huang's reinstatement would lead to less stringent enforcement, sources see little indication Nvidia will relax compliance.

*US stock futures are extending Wednesday's late recovery as global markets rebound on Thanksgiving.*

• *US Futures:* Nasdaq 100 +0.69%, S&P 500 +0.69% and Dow +0.44%.
• *Historic Recovery:* The Nasdaq recovered from a 4.6% intraday decline Wednesday to close down 0.6%, its sharpest comeback since April 2025. The Dow recorded its largest intraday recovery since February 2022.
• *Trading Schedule:* US stock and bond markets are closed for Thanksgiving. Stock markets reopen Friday for a shortened session ending at 1 PM ET.

*The Wall Street Journal highlights another potential conflict of interest at Nvidia ($NVDA), involving its former sales chief's relationship with an executive at Super Micro Computer ($SMCI).*

• *Chip Allocation:* Jay Puri led Nvidia's team responsible for allocating chips while dating Cenly Chen, Super Micro's chief growth officer, who advocated for chip supplies. They married March 7.
• *China Connection:* Puri and Jensen Huang developed a partner network including Super Micro and Megaspeed, both facing Justice Department investigations into alleged chip smuggling to China.
• *Federal Scrutiny:* FBI agents recently sought information about Chen from a person familiar with Super Micro. A March indictment alleges at least $510 million in servers were diverted to China.
• *Applied Digital Ties:* Chen helped establish Applied Digital's *($APLD)* cloud business before becoming CEO of its spin-off, ChronoScale. CEO Wes Cummins says the disclosed conflict prevented both companies from receiving certain Nvidia assistance.
• *Responses:* Chen denies involvement in chip procurement. Neither Chen nor Super Micro was charged in the indictment. Cummins was unaware of preferential treatment for Super Micro.

*Previously redacted Intel ($INTC) records became public in a federal shareholder lawsuit against the company’s board. The call notes and board minutes detail how the Trump administration pressed Intel in August 2025 to give the U.S. a roughly 10% stake in exchange for releasing $8.9 billion in grants Intel had already won.*

• *Oval Office Meeting* — Trump had called for Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan to resign over his ties to China. Tan met Trump in the Oval Office on Aug. 11.
• *Commerce Department Warning* — Commerce lawyer made the offer Aug. 18. He later told Intel’s finance chief the terms were nonnegotiable and Trump expected a Friday announcement. Intel’s notes say Shapiro warned that “rejection will have consequences” he couldn’t predict.
• *Board Decision* — Board minutes called the proposed terms unattractive. Intel ultimately agreed, and Trump valued the U.S. stake at about $11 billion. Shareholder Richard Paisner alleges the board gave in to government coercion. Intel’s lawyers say talks improved the terms and made the grants immediately available.
• *Nvidia Parallel* — WIRED cites the Intel pressure campaign as a precedent for Trump’s push to reinstate Nvidia *($NVDA)* CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia separately invested $5 billion in Intel after the U.S. stake deal.
• *Chip Sales Dispute* — Paisner separately sued for Nvidia records. Under the reported terms, Washington would receive 15% of Nvidia’s H20 chip sales to China and 25% of its H200 sales there. Paisner’s lawyers call those terms unlawful taxes. Nvidia’s lawyers deny entering an illegal agreement.

*Poland's Defence Ministry will sign a contract with Palantir ($PLTR) on Nov. 27 to supply its military with the AI-powered Maven Smart System, which will operate in Poland under the codename Saturn.*

• *Military Capabilities* — The platform combines data from drones, satellites, radars and intelligence systems to analyze battlefield conditions, identify targets and recommend operational responses to commanders.
• *NATO Integration* — Maven is used by the U.S. military, while NATO is deploying its own version. Poland tested Palantir's technology in 2024 and signed a letter of intent in October 2025.
• *Data Sovereignty* — Polish intelligence services vetted the software. Poland will retain full control over military data, system access and encryption keys. Palantir will have no remote access or permission to process military data.
• *AI Expansion* — Poland is also developing its own military AI ecosystem and plans to use EU defence loans to invest in supercomputers and AI devices capable of operating offline.

*An Iranian drone attack on Kuwait killed two Italian technicians working for German defense contractor Rheinmetall and injured a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national, according to Kuwaiti and Italian authorities. Kuwait condemned the attack as a grave breach of international law.*

• *Kuwait's Response* — The Foreign Ministry warned that continued Iranian attacks threaten regional stability and undermine diplomatic efforts, asserting Kuwait's right to defend its territory and vital infrastructure.
• *Italy's Response* — Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed condolences. Italy's Foreign Ministry confirmed the workers died in an explosion caused by the attack.
• *Regional Response* — The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) condemned the attack in the strongest terms.
• *Diplomatic Fallout* — An Italian delegation was visiting Kuwait for security talks. Al Jazeera reports the deaths could complicate efforts to restore dialogue between the US and Iran.

*Neoclouds are being told by chip suppliers that they cannot purchase Nvidia ($NVDA) GPUs if any of their computing capacity will be rented to Chinese companies, CNBC reports, citing two people familiar with the matter.*

• *Tighter Restrictions* — Nvidia previously refused to sell chips to customers renting more than 50% of their GPUs to Chinese companies. Suppliers are now reportedly ruling out any Chinese rental access following new U.S. export controls effective Nov. 19.
• *GPU Resales* — Chip suppliers are seeking alternative buyers for GPUs reportedly intended for overseas data centers serving Chinese customers.
• *Closing Loopholes* — U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the restrictions aim to prevent China from indirectly accessing advanced U.S. chips through smuggling or overseas data centers.
• *Further Restrictions* — Nvidia previously warned customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act, which has passed the House but not the Senate, could broaden U.S. authority over cloud access and expose both parties to legal action.

*Texas has been issuing data center permits after a temporary freeze, as developers rush to secure approvals before incoming Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa takes office with plans to restrict new construction.*

• *Permits Approved* — Texas has granted air pollution permits for SpaceX's $24B power plant and supercomputing facility, CloudBurst and Atlas Energy Solutions.
• *Grid Bottlenecks* — Of more than 474 GW in grid connection requests, ERCOT conditionally qualified 66.4 GW for likely initial allocations and another 127.9 GW for further study, expected to begin in April 2027.
• *Independent Power* — Texas accounts for nearly half of the 90 GW of planned self-powered U.S. data center capacity. Natural gas generator supplier ERock, whose customers include Meta, Anthropic and Microsoft, is expanding production to fulfill its $1.7B contracted backlog.

*AI is creating two challenges for the gaming industry: rising chip costs are making consoles more expensive and weakening hardware sales, while cloud gaming could eventually reduce the need for dedicated consoles. Game sales, however, remain strong.*

• *Console Slowdown* — Sony shipped 2.6M PS5 consoles in the quarter through September, down 35% YoY, while Nintendo Switch 2 sales fell 41% to 2.7M units. The six-year-old PS5 is also facing a natural decline in demand as it ages.
• *Software Strength* — GTA VI's launch may have helped lift PS5 shipments in October. Sony reported rising software sales and user engagement, while Nintendo's software sales grew nearly 20% in the six months through September, helping lift operating profit by 49%.
• *Cloud Gaming* — AI could eventually shift gaming's processing power from consoles to the cloud, allowing users to play across devices. Technical limitations, connectivity and consumer habits remain barriers.
• *AI Adoption* — Console makers are already incorporating AI to improve graphics, potentially benefiting from the technology before cloud gaming becomes a competitive threat.

*Altria ($MO) and Japan Tobacco are exploring a potential takeover of British cigarette maker Imperial Brands, Bloomberg reports, in what could be one of the UK's largest acquisitions in a decade as declining cigarette demand drives industry consolidation.*

• *Deal Structure* — Altria confirmed it is considering a joint bid with a third party. Japan Tobacco is reportedly exploring a partnership that would divide Imperial's assets geographically, potentially easing antitrust concerns.
• *Market Reaction* — Imperial shares closed 13% higher, valuing the company at £26B ($34.1B).
• *Industry Shift* — Tobacco companies are investing billions in smoke-free alternatives. Imperial plans to cut up to 4,600 jobs, or 18% of its global workforce, amid declining cigarette demand.
• *Takeover Deadline* — Imperial said it has received no approach or offer but would consider proposals. Under UK takeover rules, Altria has until Dec. 24 to announce a firm offer or walk away.

*The Netherlands vowed to resist proposed U.S. export restrictions on ASML ($ASML), warning that the MATCH Act threatens Europe's most valuable company and escalating tensions with Washington over semiconductor trade with China.*

• *Export Restrictions* — The proposed law would pressure U.S. allies to tighten chip equipment export controls, potentially expanding existing restrictions to cover sales and servicing of ASML's immersion DUV lithography machines in China.
• *Revenue Exposure* — China is expected to account for approximately 20% of ASML's revenue this year.
• *Dutch Opposition* — The Netherlands is lobbying to keep the MATCH Act out of an upcoming U.S. defense bill and pledged to resist its implementation even if passed. Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma said, “The US is not the boss of Veldhoven.”
• *EU Response* — The Netherlands is seeking coordinated EU action and will raise the issue with EU trade ministers Monday. Potential retaliatory measures include tariffs and restrictions on U.S. goods and services, risking a transatlantic trade war.

*Situational Awareness hedge fund founder Leopold Aschenbrenner predicts AI labs will reach a combined annual revenue run rate exceeding $1T by the end of 2027, while warning that superintelligent AI could erode the competitive advantages of today's technology giants.*

• *Companies at Risk* — He predicts most companies will lose “most of their value” as AI develops increasingly advanced AI systems, making employees and intellectual property obsolete. He expects Nvidia *($NVDA)*, AMD *($AMD)*, Microsoft *($MSFT)* and Apple *($AAPL)* to lose their competitive advantages, while software and IT outsourcing businesses risk replacement.
• *Elon Musk* — Aschenbrenner believes the same threat extends to the “Elonverse,” specifically referring to SpaceX and Tesla *($TSLA)*.
• *Anthropic Bet* — The fund remains “highly bullish at the IPO price” and would still make Anthropic its largest position, although portfolio rebalancing could reduce its exposure.
• *Risk Management* — After nearly collapsing during July's AI selloff, the fund restructured its portfolio, is hiring a chief risk officer and expects to resume short-selling, potentially with reduced leverage. His new mantra: “Volatility, yes; existential risk, even if we are totally wrong, never.”
• *Superintelligence* — Barring a regulatory ban, he predicts a “civilization of alien geniuses” will arrive by 2028, with hundreds or thousands of AI agents collaborating on long-term projects and advancing computing capabilities.

*“For most of the rest of the world, 2027 might be the last year that feels vaguely normal.”*

*“Perhaps the best ‘buy and hold’ asset we can come up with is the Mona Lisa,” he wrote.*

*Samsung and SK Hynix have reportedly agreed to adopt parts of a NAND chip-stacking technology pioneered by China's Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC), which says it has filed over 12,000 patent applications globally. The development highlights how rapidly the Chinese chipmaker is catching up with larger competitors, Nikkei Asia reports.*

• *Patent Licensing* — Both Korean manufacturers reportedly secured cross-licensing agreements with YMTC, primarily to avoid patent disputes. Samsung gained access to its hybrid-bonding patents in 2025.
• *Technology* — YMTC's Xtacking bonds memory cells and control circuitry manufactured on separate wafers, reducing structural constraints and enabling higher storage density as NAND exceeds 400 layers.
• *Competition* — Despite U.S. export restrictions, YMTC's global NAND revenue share rose from 11% to 14% year over year in Q2 2026, matching Kioxia and approaching Micron's ($MU) 15%.
• *Intellectual Property* — YMTC has filed over 4,000 U.S. patent applications since 2018. Samsung acknowledged the benefits of wafer bonding without confirming the agreement. SK Hynix declined to comment, while YMTC did not respond.

*Japan's largest electricity producer, JERA, is in talks with Anthropic, Meta ($META) and other U.S. tech giants to develop AI data centers alongside power plants around Tokyo, its chief executive told Nikkei.*

• *Potential Customers* — JERA has also entered discussions with Amazon *($AMZN)*, Microsoft *($MSFT)* and Google *($GOOGL)*.
• *Power Supply* — The facilities would draw electricity directly from neighboring power plants, a "behind-the-meter" arrangement designed to reduce delays associated with connecting to Japan's electricity grid.
• *Chiba Project* — JERA already has plans with Dell *($DELL)* and RHAELM to develop AI infrastructure at its Chiba Thermal Power Station, supported by up to 400 MW of power and an estimated investment exceeding $15 billion.
• *Deal Status* — Discussions remain ongoing. Customer commitments and capacity allocations have not been confirmed.

*AI data center demand has pushed some memory chip prices to 10 times their year-ago levels. Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron ($MU) cannot expand production fast enough, with shortages expected to persist at least until new factories open in 2028.*

• *Supply Outlook* — SK Hynix has sold out of DRAM and next-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM) through 2029. Micron has presold at least $150B in supply under multiyear contracts. SK Hynix's CFO expects supply constraints through 2030.
• *Industry Growth* — Counterpoint Research expects DRAM production capacity to grow 50% between 2026 and 2028. Gartner projects annual memory chip revenue will reach roughly $1.3T in 2027.
• *Contract Terms* — Citi says buyers and suppliers are moving from informal agreements toward binding contracts of up to five years, requiring 25–30% upfront payments or shared investment in new factories.
• *Supply Competition* — Tech executives say some AI giants are housing employees near Samsung factories to monitor deliveries daily, while smaller manufacturers are having orders redirected to higher-priority customers.

*Elon Musk has struggled to secure memory chips for Tesla ($TSLA) from Samsung, according to Capital Group portfolio manager Carl Kawaja, who recounted a conversation with Musk at a June conference. - WSJ*

• *Purchase Commitment* — Musk offered Samsung a long-term chip purchase commitment. Executive Chairman Lee Jae-yong reportedly said other buyers were offering the same and asked what else Musk could offer.
• *Factory Financing* — Musk then offered financing guarantees for new Samsung chip factories, but Lee again said competing customers were offering the same.
